account: A 34-year-old right-handed woman took part in a single-case proof of concept at the University of Messina and IRCCS Centro Neurolesi Bonino-Pulejo. It appears in Frontiers in Rehabilitation Sciences (2026). She has right hemiparesis, global aphasia and dysarthria from a massive left-hemisphere hemorrhage at age 19. A compact convolutional neural network in CapisciAMe used recordings from her and 69 other Italian speakers with dysarthria. She supplied 1,120 utterances of 13 target words. The methods describe 21,947 training and 1,162 validation utterances, with her November 2022 recordings held out for testing. Utterances from November 2022 (day not given, so 1 November is used) were the held-out test set. The tailored recognizer identified 680 of 936 test utterances (72.65%). Twelve rehabilitation professionals averaged 56.75% on a separate open-response listening task with 26 recordings each. No real-world communication use is documented.

ai_role.statement: The CNN classified the participant’s utterances within a 13-word vocabulary. Its 72.65% result and the listeners’ 56.75% mean came from different test formats and sample sizes. Training included other speakers, and spontaneous communication was not evaluated.
